QuestionText: HTML stands for:
Explanation: HTML: HyperText Markup Language. The standard language for creating web pages. Defines structure of content using tags/elements.

QuestionText: Which tag is used to create a hyperlink in HTML?
Explanation: Link text creates a hyperlink. 'href' = hypertext reference (the URL). 'a' stands for anchor. Target attribute: target='_blank' opens in new tab.

QuestionText: The 'href' attribute in an anchor tag specifies:
Options: A) The colour of the link
B) The URL/destination of the hyperlink
Explanation: href (hypertext reference): specifies the URL the link points to. Google creates link to Google.

QuestionText: The anchor tag <a> in HTML is used for:
Explanation: <a> = anchor element. Creates hyperlinks to: web pages, files, email addresses, phone numbers, locations. href attribute specifies destination.

QuestionText: Which HTML tag creates a table?
Explanation: HTML table structure: <table> → <tr> (table row) → <td> (table data/cell) or <th> (table header). <caption> adds table title.

QuestionText: In HTML tables, <tr> stands for:
Explanation: <tr> = table row. Contains <td> (data cells) or <th> (header cells). All table content is organised in rows and columns.

QuestionText: Which tag is used for a table header cell?
Explanation: <th> = table header cell. Bold and centered by default. <td> = table data (regular cell). <thead> groups header rows; <tbody> groups body rows.

QuestionText: The 'colspan' attribute in HTML table:
Options: B) Spans multiple columns (merges cells horizontally)
Explanation: colspan='number' makes a cell span across multiple columns. <td colspan='2'> merges 2 columns. 'rowspan' spans multiple rows (vertically).

QuestionText: Which HTML tag creates an unordered (bulleted) list?
Explanation: <ul> = unordered list (bullets). <ol> = ordered list (numbered). <li> = list item (used in both). <dl> = description list.

QuestionText: The HTML tag for the largest heading is:
Explanation: HTML headings: <h1> (largest/most important) to <h6> (smallest). <h1> is typically the page title. Use for structure/hierarchy, not just size.

QuestionText: To insert an image in HTML, which tag is used?
Explanation: inserts an image. 'src' = image source/path. 'alt' = alternative text (accessibility). is self-closing (no end tag).

QuestionText: Which HTML attribute provides alternate text for an image?
Explanation: 'alt' attribute: text displayed if image can't load; read by screen readers for accessibility. Always include alt text for images.

QuestionText: The <b> tag in HTML creates:
Explanation: <b> = bold (visual). <strong> = semantically strong (also appears bold + conveys importance to screen readers). Similarly: <i> (italic), <em> (emphasis, semantic).

QuestionText: HTML is considered a __ language, not a programming language.
Explanation: HTML = markup language. Uses tags to annotate/mark up content (structure and meaning). Not a programming language — no logic, loops, conditions. JavaScript is the programming language for web.

QuestionText: The <head> section of HTML contains:
Options: B) Metadata, title, links to CSS/JavaScript
Explanation: <head>: contains document metadata not displayed on page: <title>, <meta>, <link> (to CSS), <script> (JavaScript), <style>. <body> contains visible content.

QuestionText: CSS stands for:
Explanation: CSS: Cascading Style Sheets. Defines presentation (colours, fonts, layout) of HTML. Separates content (HTML) from presentation (CSS). 'Cascading' = rules apply in order of specificity.

QuestionText: The 'border' attribute in HTML table specifies:
Explanation: <table border='1'> adds a visible border. Border=0 (no border). Modern HTML uses CSS for styling instead: border: 1px solid black.

QuestionText: Which tag is used to create a numbered list?
Explanation: <ol> = ordered list (numbered: 1, 2, 3 or A, B, C or i, ii, iii). Use 'type' attribute to change numbering: type='A' (letters), type='i' (Roman numerals).

QuestionText: <html>, <head>, <body> tags form the basic __ of a web page.
Explanation: Basic HTML structure: <!DOCTYPE html>, <html>, <head> (metadata), <body> (visible content), </html>. This is the skeleton of every web page.

QuestionText: What does 'URL' stand for?
Explanation: URL: Uniform Resource Locator — the address of a resource on the internet. Format: protocol://domain/path. E.g., https://www.example.com/page.html.

QuestionText: HTTP stands for:
Explanation: HTTP: HyperText Transfer Protocol. Rules for transferring web pages over the internet. HTTPS: secure version (encrypted). FTP: file transfer. SMTP: email.

Explanation: rowspan='n' makes a cell span across n rows vertically. colspan spans horizontally. Used to create complex table layouts.

QuestionText: The basic structure of a table cell is represented by the tag:
Explanation: <td> = table data (cell). Contains the actual data. Multiple <td> inside a <tr> create columns. <th> for header cells.

QuestionText: Which HTML tag is used to define bold, important text semantically?
Explanation: <strong> = semantically important text (displayed bold). Screen readers emphasise it. <b> = visually bold only, no semantic meaning. <em> = emphasis (italic + semantic).

QuestionText: A hyperlink with target='_blank' opens the link in:
Explanation: target='_blank': opens link in new tab/window. target='_self': same tab (default). target='_parent': parent frame. Used when you want to keep current page open.

QuestionText: The HTML comment tag is:
Explanation: HTML comment: <!-- comment text -->. Not displayed in browser. Used for documentation, temporarily disabling code. CSS: /* comment */. JavaScript: // or /* */. Python: #

QuestionText: 'bgcolor' attribute in HTML body tag sets:
Explanation: <body bgcolor='yellow'> sets page background colour. Also: text='colour' sets text colour, link='colour' sets link colour. Modern approach: use CSS instead of HTML attributes.

QuestionText: Which HTML tag is used to create an internal page link (anchor)?
Explanation:

QuestionText: HTML stands for the language used to:
Options: B) Define the structure and content of web pages
Explanation: HTML defines structure and content. CSS defines style (presentation). JavaScript defines behaviour (interactivity). These three together form the foundation of web development.

QuestionText: The <title> tag in HTML appears in the:
Options: A) Browser tab and bookmarks (not visible on page)
Explanation: <title> in <head>: text shown in browser tab, bookmarks, search engine results. Not displayed on the web page itself.

QuestionText: The 'align' attribute in HTML can be applied to:
Options: B) Various elements (headings, paragraphs, tables) to align content
Explanation:
align attribute: left, right, center, justify. Applied to

, , etc. Modern approach: use CSS text-align property.

QuestionText: In HTML, the attribute 'cellpadding' in a table controls:
Options: B) Space within a cell (between content and border)
Explanation: cellpadding: space inside cells (between content and cell border). cellspacing: space between cells. <table cellpadding='5' cellspacing='3'>

QuestionText: What does DNS stand for in web technologies?
Explanation: DNS: Domain Name System. Translates human-readable domain names (www.google.com) to IP addresses (142.250.80.46). The 'phone book' of the internet.

QuestionText: Which HTML tag is used for a horizontal line?
Explanation: <hr> = horizontal rule. Creates a visual dividing line. Self-closing element. Attributes: width, color, size (in older HTML — use CSS in modern HTML).

QuestionText: 'mailto:' in an href attribute creates:
Options: B) A link that opens an email client with pre-filled email address
Explanation: Email us opens default email client with recipient pre-filled. Also: tel: for phone links (on mobile).

QuestionText: A web browser's main function is to:
Options: B) Request and render web pages from servers
Explanation: Browser: application that requests web pages from servers (via HTTP), receives HTML/CSS/JS, and renders them visually. Examples: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge.

QuestionText: Which is NOT a valid HTML list type?
Explanation: HTML list types: <ul> (unordered/bulleted), <ol> (ordered/numbered), <dl> (description list with terms and descriptions). There is no <rl> tag.

QuestionText: The <head> and <body> tags are contained within the:
Explanation: <html> is the root element containing all other HTML. Direct children: <head> and <body>. <!DOCTYPE html> declaration goes before <html> tag.

QuestionText: The 'cellspacing' attribute in an HTML table controls:
Explanation: cellspacing: space between adjacent cells (outside borders). cellpadding: space inside cells (inside borders). <table cellspacing='5'> adds 5px between cells.

QuestionText: 'FTP' stands for:
Explanation: FTP: File Transfer Protocol. Used to transfer files between a client and server. Used to upload web files to hosting servers. SFTP: secure version. HTTP: for web browsing.

QuestionText: A website's 'homepage' is:
Options: B) The main/starting page (index.html) of a website
C) The page with the most images
Explanation: Homepage (index.html or index.htm): the default/starting page of a website that loads when you visit the domain. Server serves index.html by default.

QuestionText: The 'font' tag in HTML specifies:
Options: B) Font face, size, and colour of text
Explanation: <font face='Arial' size='4' color='red'>Text</font> — deprecated in HTML5 (use CSS instead). Attributes: face (font family), size (1-7), color.

QuestionText: ISP stands for:
Explanation: ISP: Internet Service Provider. Company providing internet access to customers. Examples: BSNL, Airtel, Jio, ACT Fibernet. Types: dial-up, DSL, cable, fibre, mobile.

QuestionText: Which HTML tag is used to emphasise text (italic + semantic)?
Explanation: <em> = emphasis (semantic italic). Screen readers stress emphasised text. <i> = visual italic only (no semantic meaning). Similar: <strong> vs <b> for bold.

QuestionText: The 'bgcolor' table attribute changes:
Explanation: bgcolor in <table bgcolor='color'> or <tr bgcolor='color'> or <td bgcolor='color'> sets background colour. Deprecated in HTML5 — use CSS background-color property.

QuestionText: An email address link in HTML uses:
Explanation: Send email creates an email link. Clicking opens the user's default mail client with 'To' field pre-filled.
